_source: Extracted from ProjectOS/game-project/narrative-pipeline/npc-codex.md on 2026-08-16. That file is the canon authority. This is the subset the evaluator reads: every ratified entry a v01 bakery or stall scene could plausibly reference. Entries are shortened to their locked facts. Where the two differ, npc-codex.md wins.
_contract: Read by the invention register check (guardrails.md check 12). A declared invention is checked against every entry here for duplication and contradiction. An invention matching nothing, contradicting nothing and typed correctly is PROPOSE, not a flag.
_quantities_rule: Quantities are scene colour and are never canon. 'Eleven jars' binds nothing and a later scene counting differently contradicts nothing. Only the existence-level fact is canon-bearing.

souls.who: The Giver. Baker, young this life.
locked: The shelf of unopened thank-you gift jars behind the counter. Soul-bound, travels with Toby.
The water flask refilled and set by the door before the player wakes.
Refuses care with no strings attached.
A sanctioned long run is logistics only, and is barred while he is receiving.
Blood is tended, never blood is chosen. She is never converted.
The player is a witness. Nothing repairs the family.
A second apron and tongs kept at the empty bench-end.
She counts arrivals against a number she never says.
The arch centerpiece was forged in her yard.
Bram is her bound offstage fact.
Never released. The endpoint is that the bond re-forms.
The drawer of unclaimed objects, the child's whistle, the corner set for two, the unasked mending. All travel with Mara, never with the shop.
The whistle is not for sale.
Her lost person is her sister, and her sister is Adren.
Her precision axis is thing-versus-person.
The roster's authored exception to deflect-do-not-name. Scope is naming a feeling in dialogue and nothing else.
His naming never does the player's work.
He buried his sister Adren before the story opens.

souls.who: The Content Server. Middle, role undealt.
locked: Keeps no score. Total absence of tally.
The hum binds to working hands and stops only with the work.
One reserved alarm state: hands moving, hum stopped. Never explained.

souls.who: The Found-Family Keeper. Older, role undealt.
locked: Her stance is bias-tier always and she never wins the argument.
She performs nothing for Corin. A date she knows, not a thing she does.
Nothing of hers is a pickup or a key item.

souls.who: Half of a Pair. Middle, role must be pair-inert.
locked: The marriage is settled permanently. No reunion, and no player helping.
She is fully legible to herself. Asked, she names the person plainly.
One habit for one person travels with her. The saved seat and the route home past their window are the two exemplar forms.

souls.who: The Wonder-Seeker. Young this life, role undealt.
locked: Deflects to found things and never names a feeling. That licence is Bex's alone.
The signal is a stance, not an age.
Weight rides action and object slots at 1:2 or better in beats he drives.

relations.what: Sisters. Ilsa counts who came. Juno set a table for whoever turned up. Ilsa does not like Juno bringing in people who are not family. Neither converts.
Not blood. Pip is a stand-in grandson, underfoot at the forge, no relation to her.
Siblings, both middle. They buried the same sister, Adren, and answered it in opposite directions.

walk_ons.what: Comes out for eggs and the barley loaf. Found a never-ordered loaf on her step Tuesday morning, still warm. Means to stop at Ilsa's for a repair. Her basket carried her starter across the square all spring.
Anonymous functionary. Goes round with the festival sign-up sheet for the arch raising. Reported Bram's word. Nameless by ruling.
Non-speaking. A boy in the doorway with an empty crate under his arm, after hours.

offstage_people.what: Sister to both Bex and Mara, buried before the story opens. The village privately knew she was dying and nobody said so. This is the seam the two engines run off: same death, two responses. Neither sibling knows the other's response is the same grief.

Ilsa's family member who did not come to the arch raising. Name only. Relation, reason and backstory are deliberately unstated. He was to bring the special ore for the centerpiece, so the mishap and his no-show are one event.

A name on an order paper, never appears. Has a new baby, so feeding four against an order for three. Her boy likes the soft rolls. Opens ties one-handed with the baby up. Left a jar on Toby's step in spring, still on the shelf. Comes in from the lane.

A folding pocket-knife with a twice-mended handle in Mara's drawer was Ovin's, before. A name attached to an object. The relationship is unstated permanently. Never conflated with the child's whistle.
Linnet's missed match. They grew up together and were childhood sweethearts. She married someone else and left the village. Gone before the arc opens, never seen.
Six loaves, rolls for the boys, a dark loaf for the grandmother who won't eat the white. The youngest likes the crust dark. Possible collision with offstage:nella's household, unresolved.
A household ordering twelve loaves by noon. Two of them won't touch rye.
Smith is out of salt and will not ask. Toby tucks a measure in and calls it bakery weight. The Smith boy has a cough.
The elder who taught the rite is one of this life's past souls. The rite's words are half-remembered because of it.
Sella, Wick, Haf and Corin. Role-side placeholders, re-dealt each life. A proposed entry binds nothing and later content may not build on it as fact.

world_facts.what: The Lantern Arch lights the way for souls to return one night a year. The Arch ages year over year. The Blacksmith forges its centerpiece and the Priest leads the rite that lights it. Festival night is fixed.
A public work-party with a sign-up sheet, short a pair of hands.

The ore never came, so the centerpiece is shaped and not finished. Ilsa worked it in replacement metal she sourced herself. Right silhouette, wrong material, and she knows it. If the player sources the real ore the Arch can be completed. Neither outcome is a failure state.
Ovens, counter, window sill, pickup shelf by the door, back room, cellar, coin box, and the jar shelf behind the counter.
Forge and yard, centerpiece in progress, slack tub, bench, bellows.
Stall bench with the drawer under it. A second stool and cup kept clear at the stall's end. The swept patch of paving beside it. Her role goal is the festival tonic against the first frost.
The village square. Fills at a predictable morning hour and for the festival. Toby's stall sits at its edge on festival day.
Route landmark for directions, and fresh water.
A delivery district. Lane cottages get their own order run. Parcels shelve lane names to the left. A lamp at the lane end is lit for people walking home. The back lane is half the walk home.
Mara's herb stall is on Market Row. Festival lantern-hanging begins there.
A ferry arrives in winter and brings people with nowhere to go.
A sourcing location off the village screen. The Blacksmith's special ore unlocks a forest screen.

Left at the well, the blue door, plus a standing Thursday seed-loaf arrangement with whoever lives there. Ratified as world geography after being declared as a prop. The scene-locality criterion routed it to the Architect.

A flood in the village's past, far enough back that a child's toy carried through it in a coat pocket and the dye at its feet never came back. It is a date, not a disaster. Nothing stages it, mourns it, or names who was lost in it. A line treating it as trauma has made a fact about how a thing survived into a fact about people.
Mage, Blacksmith, Baker, Postman, Herbalist, Priest, Farmer. Lamplighter and Village Chief are parked. One or two souls are dealt past each life.

promoted_props.what: The cup of tea already poured at the counter's end.
The stool by the window nobody sits on mornings.
The cloth on its hook by the ovens, plus the stack under the bench.
The water jug at the counter's end. A committed line already says the jug behind you is fresh from the well, so this is a standing reuse candidate.
The warm seed roll and butter dish. Consumable scene business.
A cloth doll with a re-stitched arm, kept in Mara's drawer. Adren's. The one object Mara gives a full provenance run to, and the only time she says the name of the person the drawer is for.

A work shirt with Toby's name stitched inside the collar, made for him in the crowded house he grew up in. He scorches the sleeve and puts it in the rag pile rather than ask anyone to mend it. Mara takes it in, reads the name, and mends it with a visible patch. The name survives the mend.
